findings.title: unsubscribe dereferences a possibly-nil TopicUser record
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row, for example when they were emailed through a category watch or mailing-list mode and never visited the topic. Line 107 then raises NoMethodError, so the user gets a 500 on the unsubscribe link. Use `TopicUser.change`, or create the record, instead of assuming it exists.

findings.title: State-changing action performed on a GET request
findings.body: The unsubscribe action changes the user's notification level on a plain GET route. Mail clients, link scanners and prefetchers will trigger the change just by fetching the URL. Any third-party page can also mute or unwatch a topic through a cross-site request such as an `` tag, because there is no CSRF protection on GET. The change should only happen after an explicit POST or PUT confirmation.

findings.title: No visibility check before showing and modifying the topic
findings.body: `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` raises if the topic is not visible to the user, which is partly protected. However, the redirect branch uses `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url` before anything else, and the action then writes to TopicUser and renders the full topic view. The action also falls through to `perform_show_response`, which serialises and preloads the entire topic. A lightweight confirmation page would be safer and cheaper.

findings.title: Toggle semantics make the unsubscribe link non-idempotent
findings.body: If the level is above regular it is set to regular. Otherwise it is set to muted. Clicking the same emailed link twice, or refreshing the page, goes from tracking/watching to regular and then to muted. The user ends up muting the topic when they only meant to stop notifications. The link should set a deterministic target state.

findings.title: Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
findings.body: `tu.save!` does not set `notifications_changed_at` or `notifications_reason_id`. It also does not publish the MessageBus `notification_level_change` that `TopicUser.change` handles. The rest of the code base uses `TopicUser.change` for level changes, so the reason and timestamp can be stale and open clients are not notified.

findings.title: Explicit `render :show` added to shared perform_show_response
findings.body: Adding `render :show` to the HTML branch of `perform_show_response` is needed so `unsubscribe` finds a template. It also changes the shared path used by `show`, `wordpress` and others. It is easy to double-render or change behaviour if a caller has already rendered, and it is not covered by tests.

findings.title: Triple-stash renders unescaped HTML containing the topic title
findings.body: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` is unescaped. The text is built from `model.fancyTitle` and interpolated into an I18n string. `fancyTitle` is escaped server-side, but this relies on the title being sanitised on every path. If the title is ever not escaped, this is an XSS vector. The property name `stopNotificiationsText` is also misspelled (extra 'i').

findings.title: Route model hook has no error handling
findings.body: `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` has no catch. If the user is not logged in or cannot see the topic, the route fails without graceful handling. `afterModel` also sets `details.notificationReasonText` directly and assumes `details` exists.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation needs %{unsubscribe_url} for all callers
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` string now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Only `send_notification_email` passes it. Other callers that set `add_unsubscribe_link` and do not pass `unsubscribe_url` will get an I18n missing-interpolation error (raised in tests, rendered as a broken string in production). The spec was patched to pass a fake URL rather than handling the missing-key case in the builder.

findings.title: Multi-line unsubscribe_link is also used in plain-text body
findings.body: The locale string is now a YAML block scalar with a trailing newline and a blank line. It is appended in `body` via `body << I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', ...)` and used as markdown in the HTML part. Other locale files still lack `%{unsubscribe_url}` and the new text, so non-English locales will not show the per-topic link. Spec coverage for the new text is missing.

findings.title: Route ordering and constraint changes lack tests
findings.body: The PR reorders the routes and changes the `summary` constraints by dropping `post_number`. It adds two unsubscribe routes but there are no controller specs for unsubscribe: the redirect, a missing TopicUser, the level toggle, and an unauthenticated user. Mail template output is untested as well.
